newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico electricity agency issues $300 mln in paper.
newsitem.headline: Mexico electricity agency issues $300 mln in paper.

text.p: Mexico's Federal Electricity Commission (CFE) said it has issued $300 million worth of commercial paper.
The paper was placed by a syndicate of 29 banks from America, Europe and Asia, it said in a statement.
The government agency said that it issued the debt in order to meet its short-term capital needs that will allow it to continue with its expansion and modernization plans.

"The first issue of commercial paper of this type for the CFE was a noticeable success, and the response that it received is indicative of the financial solidity of the state-run organization ...," it said.
The CFE had originally planned to place up to $200 million of the commercial paper, but received offers of $405 million, it said.
Westdeutsche Landesbank Girozentrale (West LB) was the lead banker.
The CFE said the paper received a rating of A-1+ from Standard & Poor's and P-1 from Moody's.
